name: Airpro Technology India
sector: Networking equipment (Wi-Fi access points, Ethernet switches)
summary: Airpro Technology India, incorporated in Jaipur in 2014, designs, assembles and sells wired and wireless networking products such as Wi-Fi access points and Ethernet switches under its own brand, and plans a new factory in Jaipur. Revenue grew from ₹22.0 cr in FY24 to ₹39.1 cr in FY26 and profit after tax rose 165.5% to ₹6.08 cr in FY26, lifting the net margin to 15.6%. The ₹35.64 cr fixed-price issue at ₹99 is mostly fresh money, with ₹13 cr going to working capital and about ₹7.6 cr to the factory; at ₹99 the post-issue P/E is about 20.4x, below the two listed peers' median of 42.1x. Concentration is high: the top ten customers brought in 92.6% of FY26 revenue, the largest about 37%, all imports come from China, related-party transactions were about 30% of revenue, and promoters got shares in a March 2026 rights issue at ₹10.

fh1.finding: Revenue from operations rose from ₹22.00 cr (FY24) to ₹39.09 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 33.3%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹22.00 cr, ₹28.01 cr, ₹39.09 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.51 at 30 September 2026 (borrowings ₹8.15 cr vs net worth ₹16.09 cr), and 0.38 at the end of FY26.

fh4.finding: Borrowings fell from ₹10.52 cr (FY24) to ₹4.97 cr (FY26) while revenue rose about 78%.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹4.30 cr, ₹6.59 cr, ₹12.91 cr (FY24–FY26), and ₹16.09 cr at September 2026.

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹7.50 cr in FY26, more than the ₹6.08 cr profit (it was negative ₹0.52 cr in the six months to September 2026).

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew about 165.5% in FY26, from ₹2.29 cr to ₹6.08 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from 5.12% (FY24) to 8.18% (FY25) and 15.56% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on equity was 62.41% in FY26, helped by a small equity base.

pr5.finding: FY26 net margin of 15.56% vs a peer median of about 5.0% (D-Link India 6.60%, Black Box 3.44%).

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 20.4x (₹123.77 cr market cap on 1,25,01,970 shares at ₹99 ÷ ₹6.08 cr FY26 PAT) vs a peer median of 42.1x (D-Link India 13.92x, Black Box 70.23x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.75x (₹123.77 cr ÷ ₹45.0 cr, i.e. ₹16.09 cr September 2026 net worth + ₹28.91 cr fresh issue) vs a peer median of 7.61x (D-Link India 2.87x, Black Box 12.35x).

va3.finding: Post-issue market cap to FY26 revenue is about 3.17x (₹123.77 cr ÷ ₹39.09 cr) vs about 0.92x for D-Link India and 2.42x for Black Box (P/E × net margin), a median of about 1.67x.

va4.finding: A rights issue on 17 March 2026 allotted 2,34,940 shares at ₹10, about 90% below the ₹99 issue price (a 7:2 bonus followed on 30 March 2026).

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 68.12% after the issue, down from 95.00%.

pg2.finding: The draft prospectus states the promoters have not pledged any shares.

pg3.finding: Related-party transactions were ₹6.32 cr in the six months to September 2026, 30.01% of revenue, including ₹4.55 cr of sales to Airpro FZ-LLC.

pg4.finding: Three proceedings totalling ₹30.95 lakh are pending against promoters or directors: one criminal case (₹16.19 lakh) and two direct tax cases (₹14.76 lakh).

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹6.73 cr (6,80,000 shares), about 18.9% of the ₹35.64 cr issue.

is2.finding: The ₹35.64 cr issue is about 28.8% of the ₹123.77 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: Selling promoters' average cost is ₹2.42 (Deepak Jain) and ₹1.79 (Roopali Bhansali) a share, so ₹99 is about 41–55x their cost.

up1.finding: ₹7.57 cr (machinery ₹2.00 cr, land balance ₹0.60 cr, factory building ₹4.97 cr) for the Jaipur factory is about 26.2% of the ₹28.91 cr fresh issue; ₹13 cr goes to working capital.

up2.finding: None of the fresh issue is earmarked for repaying debt.

up3.finding: General corporate purposes are ₹4.34 cr, about 15.0% of the ₹28.91 cr gross fresh proceeds, right at the 15% limit.

up4.finding: No proceeds go to repaying loans; the draft prospectus states no part of the net proceeds will be paid to the promoters.

lg1.finding: Three proceedings against the company total ₹0.76 lakh, far below 1% of the ₹16.09 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: One criminal case (₹16.19 lakh) is pending against a promoter or director; there are no criminal or regulatory cases against the company.

lg3.finding: The draft prospectus shows nil contingent liabilities for every period to 31 December 2025.

rk1.finding: The top ten customers brought in 92.64% of FY26 revenue, and the largest customer 36.87% in the six months to September 2026.

rk2.finding: The largest supplier accounted for 58.62% of purchases in the nine months to December 2025, and all imports (71% of purchases to September 2026) come from China.

rk3.finding: Incorporated on 17 February 2014, so about 12 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: The restated accounts show no adjustments for audit qualifications in any period, and the earlier auditor gave unmodified opinions.
